Adlai Stevenson Sr. was the twenty-third Vice President of the United States, serving under Grover Cleveland from eighteen ninety-three to eighteen ninety-seven. During this second Cleveland administration, the nation faced the Panic of eighteen ninety-three, a severe economic depression marked by labor unrest including the Pullman Strike. As Vice President during this turbulent period, Stevenson represented the free-silver wing of the Democratic Party, opposing Cleveland's commitment to the gold standard. This ideological tension deepened divisions within the party. Before becoming Vice President, he served as a U.S. Congressman from Illinois, bringing agrarian and populist sympathies to national politics that made him a natural running mate for Cleveland despite their differences. Stevenson was an early supporter of expansionist foreign policy and the Spanish-American War, positions that foreshadowed American imperial ambitions. He ran unsuccessfully for Governor of Illinois and built a significant political machine in state Democratic politics. Late in his career, he served as U.S. Minister to Belgium, representing American interests in the years before World War I. His grandson, Adlai Stevenson II, became a prominent twentieth-century Democrat and two-time presidential candidate, reviving the family name in politics. Though the McKinley era eclipsed his political fortunes, Stevenson remained a prominent Democratic elder before his death in nineteen fourteen.
